name: sort
algorithm: Sort n u64 keys in four patterns per round (splitmix64-mixed random keys, reversed, a sawtooth of period 1000, 16 distinct keys), each sorted ascending by the language's std unstable sort and checked; rounds times (README.md).

skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; sorting has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own sort algorithm; the checksum (the weighted sum of each sorted pattern, 0xdead if out of order) checks every result
notes: Unstable sorts (B20): mk Slice.Sort (pdqsort, comparator a const fn argument); c qsort, an indirect comparator through a function pointer; rust sort_unstable (ipnsort); zig std.sort.pdq; go slices.Sort (pdqsort); cs MemoryExtensions.Sort (IntroSort).
